title: In-Memory Arithmetic: Enabling Division with Stochastic Logic
problem: Efficient hardware division has been a long-standing challenge; traditional binary approaches require multiple cycles and complex control logic. Emerging in-memory computing faces additional obstacles: noise sensitivity, process variation, and the inherent difficulty of binary operations in noisy substrates.
motivation: In-memory computing is gaining adoption for energy efficiency and parallelism, but arithmetic operations (especially division) remain problematic; stochastic computing offers inherent fault tolerance making it attractive for noisy in-memory substrates.
method: The approach uses stochastic computing (SC) to implement division within an MTJ-based in-memory architecture; SC represents numbers as bitstreams and performs arithmetic through simple logic operations, naturally tolerating noise. MTJ memory provides the substrate for logic-in-memory operations, reducing the data movement penalty.
key_novelty: Application of stochastic computing to in-memory division leveraging MTJ crossbars, achieving fault tolerance against process variation and noise inherent in emerging memory substrates.
contributions: Stochastic computing-based division architecture for in-memory computation
MTJ-based memory crossbar substrate for logic-in-memory division
Demonstrated robustness across process variation conditions
Real-world application to Retinex Algorithm for image enhancement

metrics.other: robustness demonstrated across process variation conditions

limitations: Throughput-precision trade-offs and convergence speed not quantified; comparison with other SC-based arithmetic not provided.
primary_theme: stochastic in-memory division for fault-tolerant analog/near-analog computing
